newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-TROUBLED FRANCE SEEK REVENGE OVER SPRINGBOKS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TROUBLED FRANCE SEEK REVENGE OVER SPRINGBOKS.

text.p: France must overcome the loss of no fewer than six of their first-choice players as they attempt to take revenge over world champions South Africa in the first of two rugby union tests on Saturday

"We have a lot of absentees, and not minor ones, but we still aim at winning that match," said coach Jean-Claude Skrela after seeing Philippe Saint-Andre, Olivier Merle, Olivier Roumat, Thomas Castaignede, Alain Penaud and Jean-Louis Jordena all withdraw through injury.

"All these injuries are the result of too many high level matches, especially in the European Cup," said team manager Jo Maso. "But we are still looking forward to that match and I am sure that the players will give their all."
France and South Africa, in many ways two extremes in the rugby world, have not clashed since their memorable World Cup semifinal in Durban in June, 1995.

The Springboks won a close contest in pouring rain 19-15 and went on to beat the All Blacks in the final at Ellis Park while France had to be content with beating England to take third place in the tournament.

"The French have not forgotten that match and they will be seeking revenge, no doubt," said South African winger James Small, who played the game in Durban and will be on the pitch in Bordeaux on Saturday.
The visitors started their tour of France in disastrous fashion by losing their first match 30-22 to the French Barbarians in Brive last Saturday.
But they recovered some pride on Tuesday by scoring five tries in an impressive display of powerful rugby to beat a French regional selection 36-20 in Lyon.

Those two matches were played by a reserve team while the team for the first test, similar to the one who recently won two tests against the Pumas in brilliant fashion, was left to concentrate on Saturday's match.
Coming from sunny Argentina, the South Africans experienced wintry conditions in France with cold rain and even snow and were forced to modify their training programme slightly.

Now captained by Natal number eight Gary Teichmann, the Springboks have suffered since their World Cup triumph and this year lost a series for the first time to their bitterest ennemies, the New Zealand All Blacks.

"We are under a lot of pressure because everybody wants to beat us," said gifted scrumhalf Joost van der Vesthuizen. "We've had some problems but I believe we are just as strong as when we won the World Cup."
Skrela, who named veteran number eight Abdelatif Benazzi as the team's captain following the withdrawal of Saint-Andre, was forced to build a young and largely unexperienced side.
"It is a very young team and it's probably the first time we launch such an unexperienced side at such a level but we had no choice," he said.

Centre Guillaume Bouic, who learned his trade alongside great Philippe Sella at Agen, will earn his first cap by replacing Castaignede while flyhalf Laurent Mazas, who comes in for Penaud, has only been selected once before.

"They are good players," said Springboks assistant coach Nick Mallett, who saw them both in action with the French Barbarians last Saturday. "The French will field a strong side and we're expecting a tough match."

South Africa traditionally rely on the power of their forwards while France have a reputation for fluent, open rugby. But the introduction of new rules has forced the Springboks to bring some variety to their game while the French now clearly understand the importance of a strong pack.

"To win a match like this one, you must be ready to suffer," said Benazzi. "It's never going to be easy against the Springboks but the circumstances have brought us closely together and I believe we stand a chance."
Teams:

Fraance: 15-Jean-Luc Sadourny, 14-Richard Dourthe, 13-Guillaume Bouic, 12-Stephane Glas, 11-David Berty, 10-Laurent Mazas, 9-Philippe Carbonneau, 8-Thierry Labrousse, 7-Abdelatif Benazzi (captain), 6-Philippe Benetton, 5-Fabien Pelous, 4-Hugues Miorin, 3-Franck Tournaire, 2-Marc de Rougemont, 1-Christian Califano.

South Africa : 15-Andre Joubert, 14-James Small, 13-Japie Mulder, 12-Hennie Le Roux, 11-Jacques Olivier, 10-Henry Honniball, 9-Joost van der Westhuizen, 8-Gary Teichmann (cap), 7-Andre Venter, 6-Ruben Kruger, 5-Mark Andrews, 4-Kobus Wiese, 3-Adrian Garvey, 2-James Dalton, 1-Dawie Theron.
